title: CoT-Monitor Stress Test: Minimal Obfuscation Pressure Threshold

original_idea.body: CoT-Monitor Stress Test. Problem: no public graded benchmark measures the minimal prompt-pressure level at which a CoT monitor's detection accuracy collapses per open model. Direction: define an obfuscation-instruction ladder, run an LLM-judge monitor on a task with a detectable shortcut, find the pressure rung where detection fails; report a per-model evasion threshold.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: monitor-evasion thresholds probe fragility of a leading safety mechanism; targets >1yr threat.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Obfuscation ladder + LLM-judge monitor; inherited methodology.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused per-model evasion-threshold metric; shortcut task adds scope.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Foundational long-horizon monitor-robustness work, lab-independent third-party scrutiny.

novelty.reasoning: Graded obfuscation-pressure work exists; per-model evasion-threshold benchmark may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Graded obfuscation pressure is studied; a public per-model evasion-threshold benchmark is plausibly open.
